title: Improvement of the Moral Qualities — Hebrew and English excerpts
attribution: Solomon ibn Gabirol; historical Hebrew translation by Judah Ibn Tibbon; Hebrew Wikisource contributors (see revision history); English translation by Stephen S. Wise, 1902, via Sefaria.
changes: Selected and resegmented Hebrew passages and paired 39 with corresponding passages from the separately edited Wise English version; retained further paragraphs from five unfinished Wikisource pages without English alignment. Source segments were joined and split at reviewed paragraph boundaries; relevant English headings and heading notes were omitted. No original translation or new OCR was produced.
coverage: Partial medieval Hebrew translation by Judah Ibn Tibbon from five cited Wikisource pages, each marked unfinished. The pages contain text under all twenty topics, but whole-work completeness and proofreading are not established. 39 passages in selected topics are paired with Wise’s 1902 English; remaining Hebrew passages are not paired here. The Judeo-Arabic original is not included. These are different translations, with variants and omissions.
limitations: The Wikisource project does not specify its underlying printed edition on its project page. The historical scan is a separate witness, not established as the source of the transcription. Hebrew and English were compared for these excerpts only; edition variants and jurisdiction-specific public-domain status remain relevant.

alignmentNotes.topic2: Four Hebrew paragraphs paired with English source segments 1–6; segments 5 and 6 split at reviewed sentence boundaries. Heading and heading notes not reproduced. Original and English are different translations and variants remain.
alignmentNotes.topic3: Two Hebrew paragraphs paired with English source segments 1–7; segment 5 split before Aristotle. Heading omitted. Hebrew and English are different translations and variants remain.
alignmentNotes.topic4: Five Hebrew paragraphs paired with English source segments 1–2, split at reviewed sentence boundaries. Heading omitted; separate Hebrew closing line is unpaired. Different source editions may vary.
alignmentNotes.topic5: Two Hebrew paragraphs paired with English source segments 1–4, with segment 4 split before the discussion of desire for greatness. Heading omitted. Different source editions may vary.
alignmentNotes.topics6-7-11-18: Whole Hebrew topic paragraphs matched by content to English source segments after the heading. The historical translations differ: topic 6 has a different verb about hatred, topic 7 includes an extra biblical citation in Hebrew, topic 11 references a parallel prophetic verse, and topic 18 includes variant wording about prodigality. These are source-aligned editions, not identical word-for-word translations; headings and their notes are omitted.
alignmentNotes.topics8-9-12: Three Hebrew topic paragraphs paired with the corresponding English source text after its heading. Hebrew transition notes are unpaired. Topic 9 differs on the circumstances provoking laughter; different translations can contain other variants or omissions.
alignmentNotes.topics13-14-17: Three whole Hebrew topic paragraphs paired with the corresponding English source segments. Topic 13 omits one temperament description in English; topics 14 and 17 contain extra poems or examples in English. Headings omitted; other textual variants may remain.
alignmentNotes.topics15-20: Two topic paragraphs paired with English segments 1–4. Topic 15 contains an English poem marked absent in Hebrew. Topic 20 excludes an English concluding passage absent from the Hebrew; the Hebrew closing prayer and colophon have no matching English here. Heading notes omitted.
alignmentNotes.topics10-19: Three grief paragraphs aligned to Wise segments 1–9, splitting segments 2 and 6 at reviewed narrative boundaries; two valor paragraphs aligned to segments 1–2 and 3–4. Headings omitted, and variants or material absent in either translation may remain.
alignmentNotes.topic1Additional: Four later Hebrew paragraphs paired to Wise segments 5–15. Wise segment 5 split at the turn to dangers; the section on ancient sages excludes an Arabic poem absent from the Hebrew. The anecdote about an arrogant man differs: the Hebrew mentions shoes and English a wagon. The source placeholder for the missing poem is deliberately unpaired.
alignmentNotes.unpairedPositions: Topic 16 opening remains unpaired because Hebrew says red bile while Wise says yellow gall; its remaining passage is paired. Other unpaired positions are a missing-poem notice and closing or transition lines.
alignmentNotes.topic16: Split the Hebrew and English openings at their first substantive sentence boundary; excluded the conflicting red/yellow bile introduction from the paired English and retained both Hebrew opening and closing line without paired English. The rest is paired to Wise segments 1–3. Other source variations remain possible.
